titular: Bitcoin funds see outflows for a seventh day, losing $643.6m in a week
resum: New development: US spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) saw $185.45m of outflows on Friday, a seventh straight day, bringing the week's total to $643.6m. Bitcoin traded near $69,000, its lowest level since August, down a little over 6% in 24 hours.
per_que_importa: These funds are the gateway to bitcoin for many traditional investors; when money leaves them, the price tends to suffer. It is a reminder that this is a very volatile asset with no guarantee scheme to cover losses.

titular: Thailand wants to cap stablecoin transfers at about $148,000 a day
resum: Thailand's securities regulator is proposing a daily limit of 5 million baht (about $148,000) on some transfers of stablecoins, cryptocurrencies pegged to the dollar, to fight money laundering. Transfers between a user's own accounts would be exempt, and comments can be submitted until 26 November.
per_que_importa: Stablecoins are increasingly used to move money quickly between countries, which also attracts criminals. Each country decides how to control them, and these rules could end up inspiring other regulators.

titular: The US approves its first final rules for stablecoin issuers
resum: The OCC, one of the US bank supervisors, has approved a rule requiring the stablecoin issuers it oversees to meet reserve, redemption, capital and risk management standards. It will apply once the GENIUS Act takes effect on 18 January 2027.
per_que_importa: A stablecoin is only worth a dollar if the issuer really has the money to pay it back. These rules aim to guarantee that, but a stablecoin is still not a bank deposit protected by a guarantee scheme.

titular: SoFi bank brings its stablecoin to a new payments network
resum: SoFiUSD, the stablecoin issued by US lender SoFi Bank, now runs on the Polygon network, its third blockchain after Ethereum and Solana. Customers can buy, hold and convert it in the SoFi app, and each unit can be exchanged for one dollar.
per_que_importa: A regulated bank issuing its own dollar-pegged cryptocurrency brings this technology closer to everyday payments. SoFi itself warns it is not a bank deposit and so does not have the same protection.

titular: About $300,000 in tokens stolen from the Edel platform
resum: An attacker made off with EDEL tokens worth about $300,000 and sold them on the market; it is not yet known how they got in. The team is working with authorities and exchanges to block the funds, and some have already frozen part of them.
per_que_importa: Thefts from crypto platforms are common and, unlike with a bank, there is no guarantee scheme to return the money. Anyone holding assets there depends on the platform being willing and able to cover the losses.
